column6: stem "Nearly every connected space is path-connected" (key false) made the key wrong; restored "Every"
garbled "Most connected topological space" (key false); restored "Every"
final sentence said the box topology is "strictly coarser"; it is finer

stem "Most surjective continuous map" restored to "Every"; explanation said circle topology is "finer" and that open sets of S¹ have non-open preimages (impossible for continuous f); now coarser / non-open sets with open preimages
answer said a finer topology "would require q to be an open map" (it would make q discontinuous); explanation said coarser topology declares U "closed" (should be "not open")
same "declare some set U closed" error; now "not open"
T1 ⊂ T2 ⊂ T3 ⊂ T4 states class inclusion backwards; now T4 ⟹ T3 ⟹ T2 ⟹ T1

regularity is preserved under continuous images (unlike T₂) is false (any space is a continuous image of a discrete space); replaced with products and subspaces. Note: file has Explainer before Questions (old order, not moved)
T₂ ⊂ T₃ ⊂ T₄ and "T₀ ⊂ … ⊂ T₄" reversed class inclusion; now implication arrows
garbled "if and mainly if most point"; restored "if and only if every point"
garbled "Most T₁ space is Hausdorff" (key false); restored "Every". Note: old How/Misconceptions are prose (not bullets) and Explainer precedes Questions; left as is
all spaces that arise in analysis and geometry are metric spaces overstated (now "many"); "T₁ ⊂ T₂ ⊂ T₃ ⊂ T₄" reversed (now implication chain)
Urysohn nesting stated as U_r ⊆ closure(U_s); correct condition is closure(U_r) ⊆ U_s
sufficient (and necessary): T₂ is not necessary for unique sequential limits (cocountable topology on an uncountable set); removed "(and necessary)"

stem "Nearly every Hausdorff space" restored to "Every"; explanation called the two axes of the Sorgenfrey plane disjoint closed sets (they meet at the origin); now rational vs irrational points of y = −x
complement of {x} described as an "intersection" of open sets; it is a union

closed and bounded ⟹ compact is special to ℝⁿ overstated (other proper metric spaces have it); now "holds in ℝⁿ but fails in general". Note: old Explainer calls uncountable products "Tychonoff spaces" (misnomer), left
cited uncountable products as sequentially compact but not compact (it is the reverse); now [0, ω₁) for that direction, products for the other
garbled "should have trivial πₙ for most n"; restored "must … for all n ≥ 1"
garbled "exactly of most finite intersections"; now "the finite intersections"
garbled "is expected to also be open"; restored "must also be open"
bullet 2 (extensions stay in [−1,1]) is a weak but plausible misconception; kept. Note: old q:0 has two true options (A and B)
garbled "on most of X"; restored "on all of X"
one characterization of metrizable spaces is that they are normal is false; now "every metrizable space is normal"
garbled "they is expected to be homeomorphic"; restored "must be"

global topology can typically be determined by examining the charts in its atlas is arguably true (atlas with overlaps determines it), so key false did not fit; now "any single chart", matching the explanation

stem "Nearly every set X has exactly one topology" restored to "Every"; explanation "any set carries at least two topologies" false for sets with ≤1 point; now "with at least two points … distinct". Note: Explainer precedes Questions (old order)
new bullet 2 is right and exposed an old error below. Note: Core Idea omits the T₁ requirement (indiscrete 2-point space is second-countable, normal, not metrizable); left
garbled "Most second-countable space"; restored "Every"
both claimed the unscaled map x ↦ (fₙ(x)) lands in ℓ²; added the 1/n scaling
garbled "applies to most Hausdorff spaces"; restored "all"
torus paragraph called U ∩ V a circle and "simply connected"; it is an annulus with π₁ = ℤ whose core loop is aba⁻¹b⁻¹ in U
